programme.title: Luontoretkellä
programme.desc: 3/5. Miksi luonnonvaraiset eläimet eivät nuku öisin? Mitä ne oikein puuhaavat? Kari Toft tarkkailee nälkäisiä jäniksiä ja epätavallisen ketterää mäyrää. Sarja esittelee norjalaisten tv-katsojien videoita kohtaamisista luonnonvaraisten eläinten kanssa.

programme.title: Eräelämää
programme.desc: Kausi 2, 5/8. Tällä kertaa Peter Ekeström ja Evelina Åslund Bäck suuntaavat Smålandin metsiin, missä he osallistuvat metsäkauriin ajometsästykseen dreevereiden kanssa. Ruotsalainen metsästysohjelma.

programme.title: Ystävä sä lapsien
programme.desc: Jos uskonnollisessa yhteisössä elävät vanhemmat eivät pidä lapsistaan huolta, kenen tehtävä on auttaa lapsia? Knutby Filadelfia-seurakunnassa kasvanut Linnéa käy vanhassa koulussaan. Miksi kukaan ei aikoinaan puuttunut asioihin?

programme.title: Kuin kaikki muut
programme.desc: Down-tytöt Madde ja Matilda esiintyvät ensi kertaa yleisön edessä. Pitävätkö heidän hermonsa - ja mahtaako yleisö pitää heistä? Anders on risteilyllä Cecilian kanssa. Hän ostaa nuuskaa ja tanssii baarissa. Ja kuinka mahtoi käydä Robinille ja Marialle, jotka tapasivat sokkotreffeillä? Löysivätkö he rakkauden vai jatkuuko kumppanin etsiminen? Tuotanto: Olof Film, 2020.

programme.title: Elias on pelastettava
programme.desc: Poliisi on löytänyt kahdeksanvuotiaan Eliaksen ja ottanut kiinni pojan äidin. Pojan isää vastaan vihakampanjaa ajanut ryhmä ei aio silti antaa periksi. Kun äiti tuodaan oikeuden eteen, isää odottaa uusi yllätys. Ruotsalainen dokumenttisarja tapahtumasarjasta, joka on kuohuttanut satojatuhansia ihmisiä sosiaalisessa mediassa, mutta johon toimittajat eivät ole tätä ennen tarttuneet. Tuotanto: SVT, 2020.

programme.title: Tanskalainen maajussi
programme.desc: Kasvihuoneen tomaatit kypsyvät, ja Frank pääsee maistiaisille. Rasvapuristimet on puhdistettava ja Frank laittaa seetrilastuja myllyn akseliin. Kasvimaa on taas veden vallassa.

programme.title: Andersin kanssa kalassa
programme.desc: 12/12. Anders lähtee Norjaan Hitraan kalastamaan Atlantin syvissä vesissä. Hän kokeilee myös kalastamista oikein isolla haavilla Tukholman keskustassa.

programme.title: Historia: Cambridgen vakoojat
programme.desc: Miten Cambridgen yliopiston opiskelijatovereista tuli vakoojia, jotka toimivat Neuvostoliiton hyväksi 1930-60-luvuilla? Ohjelmassa seurataan ennen kaikkea Kim Philbyä, joka paljastettuaan pakeni Neuvostoliittoon, missä hän kuoli alkoholisoituneena vuonna 1988. Tuotanto: Wingspan/ITV, Iso-Britannia 2022

programme.title: Kaipaus: Kangastus (7)
programme.desc: Nina elää kiihkeässä rakkaussuhteessa netissä tapaamansa miehen kanssa. Pari aikoo ostaa yhdessä talon Provencesta, mutta huijaako mies Ninaa raha-asioissa? Käsikirjoittaja ja ohjaaja: Anna Blom. Tuotanto: Ja Media Production, 2022.

programme.title: Kohti Tanssin taloa

programme.title: Kaamos - suomalaisen metallin viisi vuodenaikaa
programme.desc: Kuinka paljon sä haluat tätä? Traagisista tarinoista ja varoittavista esimerkeistä huolimatta raskas musiikki vaatii usein veronsa. Unelman toteutumisen ja rundaamisen sietämätön raskaus, päihdesekoilut, terveysongelmat ja supertähtien yhteentörmäykset. Hiljaisuuden päättävä sovinto, tosiystävyys, musiikin voima sekä folkmetallin parantava huumori ja sankarienergia. Mukana mm. Battle Beast, Noora Louhimo, Sentenced And Miika Tenkula, Children of Bodom, Bodom After Midnight And Alexi Laiho, Silke Yli-Sirniö, Joel Hokka, Tarja Turunen, Marco Hietala ja Ensiferum. programme.title: Kino: Peto (16)
programme.desc: Vuosi 2044: tekoäly hallitsee stoalaisen yhteiskunnan kaikkia puolia ihmisten rutiininomaisesti ”pyyhkiessä” tunteitaan. Gabrielle (Léa Seydoux) rakastuu toistuvasti Louisin (George MacKay) eri inkarnaatioihin. Aluksi belle époque -aikakauden Pariisissa Louis on brittimies, joka houkuttelee Gabriellea pois kylmästä avioliitosta, ja sitten 2000-luvun alussa Los Angelesissa hän on häiriintynyt amerikkalainen tavoitteenaan epämääräinen kosto. Saako Gabrielle täydellisen yhteyden Louisiin nykyhetkellä vai ovatko he tuomitut toistamaan aiemmat kohtalonsa?Taiteellisesti korkeatasoisista töistään tunnettu ranskalainen huippuohjaaja Bertrand Bonello (House of Tolerance, Saint Laurent, Nocturama) on luonut Henry Jamesin vuosisadan vaihteen novellista The Beast in the Jungle hienostuneen scifi-eepoksen, jossa hiipii pelko ja mysteerin tuntu. Peto kuvaa koskettavalla tavalla ihmiskunnan taistelua dissosiatiivista identiteettiä ja tunteetonta olemassaoloa vastaan.

programme.desc: Dokumenttielokuva kertoo luopumisesta ja uuteen sopeutumisesta pitkän ja menestyksekkään uran jälkeen. Päähenkilö, 73-vuotias tanssija ja balettimestari Jarmo Rastas, on lopettamassa uraansa Suomen kansallisbaletissa, ja pohtii työn jälkeistä elämää ja omaa identiteettiään. Jarmon tarinaa peilataan myös kolmen tanssijan - Nina Hyvärisen, Tiina Myllymäen ja Michal Krčmářin - kanssa, jotka alansa huippuina tuntevat myös uusien alkujen haasteet. Aviomies hakkaa ja haukkuu, mutta autokorjaamolla työskentelevä lempeä nuoruudenrakastettu pehmentää pelon sävyttämää arkea. Kun posti tuo yllättävän kirjeen, kuinka pitkään nurkkaan ajettu nainen enää alistuu asemaansa itsestäänselvyytenä?Ainahan on huominen on kaikkien aikojen tuottoisin naisen ohjaama italialainen elokuva – kotimaassaan vuonna 2023 jopa katsotumpi kuin Barbie! Italian elokuvatoimittajat valitsivat elokuvan vuoden parhaaksi, samoin sekä tuomaristo että yleisö Rooman elokuvafestivaalilla. Göteborgin elokuvafestivaalilla se palkittiin vuoden parhaana kansainvälisenä elokuvana.

Onko se jokin suuren suuri asia, niin kuin vaikka tulivuori tai valtameri, vai pienenpieni kuten hiekanjyvänen tai lumihiutale? programme.desc: Monsterimuistelopäivänä Gustav tahtoo jutella esi-isilleen. Mutta onkohan Tuiskulassa asuminen tehnyt monsterista ihan nössön?

programme.title: Poika, tyttö, koira, kissa, hiiri ja juusto (7)

programme.title: Jumppahetki
programme.desc: Sykettä nostattava koko kehon jumppa huivin tai kepin kanssa. Liikkeet voi tehdä myös istuen.

programme.title: Bussikuski
programme.desc: Said on keski-ikäinen mies, joka haluaa kerran elämässään tehdä juuri sen, mitä itse haluaa. Vastoin lähimpien neuvoja Said päättää jättää vakituisen työpaikkansa ja lähteä opiskelemaan. Ohj. Mohamed El Aboudi.

programme.title: Rohkea rokan syö
programme.desc: Suomessa on totuttu syömään kouluissa ilmainen ateria jo vuosikymmenten ajan. Kouluruokailun ihanuutta ja kurjuutta muistelevat 60-luvun koululainen Maija Toivanen Inarista ja 70-luvun koululainen Jyrki Torni Helsingistä. Makaroonivellistä on pitkä matka spagettiin ja erilaisiin dieettivaihtoehtoihin. Käsik. And ohj. Susanna Kuronen.

programme.title: SuomiLOVE
programme.desc: Sonja Lumme, Taiska, Janna, Susanna Haavisto And Eija Ahvo, Jarkko Martikainen, Klamydia, Nikke Ankara, LOVEband, Johanna Iivanainen ja Osmo Ikonen. Juontajina Jenni Pääskysaari ja Mikko Leppilampi.

programme.title: Varikkounelmia
programme.desc: Tiian SM-kisoihin on aikaa vain 2 viikkoa. Nooran kalenteri ratkeaa liitoksistaan. Milja on saanut moottoriurheiluinnostuksen kotoaan. Elena pääsee treenaamaan itse kasaamansa mimmitiimin kera.

programme.title: Ammatti: kirjailija: Aila Meriluoto
programme.desc: Äitini oli sitä mieltä, että minusta tuli runoilija, kun minä kolhaisin pääni vauvana. Se ei ollut kovin suotavaa, että rupeaa haihattelemaan, ryhtyy runoilijaksi tai kirjailijaksi, sanoo Aila Meriluoto (1924 - 2019). Runoilijasta tuli sodan kokeneen sukupolven ääni.

programme.title: Naissotilaat
programme.desc: Pirita kotiutuu ja hyvästelee haikeana Pasi-koiran. Myös Miisan, Moonan ja Jennin taival armeijan vihreissä lähestyy loppuaan. Jos armeija tekee pojasta miehen, mitä se teki tytöistä?

programme.title: Eränkävijät
programme.desc: Sørøyan saari ei ole päästänyt Mehtämikkoa helpolla, mutta edessä on monta lupaavaa kalapaikkaa, jotka motivoivat haasteiden yli. Käsivarren erämaassa Aki ja Äijä saavat kalastuspäivälleen aktiivisen aloituksen. Manu on saapunut Tenojoelle auttamaan jokeen nousseen vieraslajin, kyttyrälohen, kanssa. Teemu ja Mima puolestaan ovat lähteneet Hausjärvelle seuraamaan kosteikon kunnostustyötä, jolla tavoitellaan parempaa elinympäristöä hädässä oleville lintulajeille. Lakselvalla Emma ja Jouni kartoittavat uusia kalapaikkoja. Tarkoitus on myös yhyttää paikalle saapuneet kalakaverit.

programme.title: Tiettömän taipaleen takana
programme.desc: Skjæløy-lautta kulki vuosikymmenien ajan Helgeroan kylän lähisaariin Oslonvuonossa . Se mahdollisti toimeentulon Stokkøyan harvoille asukkaille. Mutta nyt lautta on maannut laiturissa jo pari vuotta. Johansenin perhe haluaa tehdä kaikkensa saadakseen lautan takaisin liikenteeseen.

programme.title: Tanskalainen maajussi
programme.desc: Frank viimeistelee keittiön uudet laatikot steariinilla, ja nyt ne liukuvat kuin unelma. Solveig-hevosen valjaat ovat menneet rikki, ja apua niiden korjaamiseen haetaan Ruotsista asti.

programme.title: Huutokauppakesä
programme.desc: Kaksi kahden hengen joukkuetta lähtee huutokauppaan saman rahasumman kanssa. Kumpi pareista tekee parempia löytöjä? Bispgårdenissa asuvat sisarukset Marianne Eriksson Holmberg ja Ewa Eriksson saavat vastaansa tukholmalaiset Tihna Ivarssonin ja Mandie Söderströmin. Huutokauppa käydään Frändeforsissa Länsi-Ruotsissa. Ohjelman juontaa Sofia Rågenklint, ja tuomareina sekä tavaroiden arvon määrittelijöinä toimivat Maria Granström ja Mats Bergstrand. Ruotsalainen huutokauppasarja.

programme.title: Talot huokuvat historiaa
programme.desc: Hallandin Grimetonissa sijaitseva Torstorpin tila on peräisin keskiajalta. Nina ja Svante, jotka asuvat siellä teini-ikäisten lastensa kanssa, ovat kuulleet tarinoita sieppauksesta sekä esiin kaivetusta ja siirretystä ruumiista, mutta onko huhuissa perää? Antiikkiesineiden tuntija Rickard Thunér sukeltaa arkistoihin etsimään heille vastauksia. Rakennustutkija Erika Åberg puolestaan auttaa perhettä löytämään ruokasaliin uuden väripaletin ja energiaa säästävät verhot.

programme.title: Mielettömät leikit
programme.desc: Miksi jotkut haluavat urheilla vaarallisissa paikoissa? Mikä oikeuttaa leikin, mitä on egoismi ja kuka asettaa rajat? Kysymyksiin vastaavat Karina Hollekim, Osku Siivonen ja Pati Blom. Toimittaja: Ilse Klockars, 2009.

programme.title: Lentopallon EM
programme.desc: Lentopallon miesten EM-kisojen välieräottelu. Selostus: Johannes Oikarinen, asiantuntijana Timo Tolvanen, Torino, Italia.

programme.title: Uefan jalkapallon U21 EM-karsinta: Suomi - Espanja
programme.desc: U21-EM-karsinnat kohti kesällä 2027 Albaniassa ja Serbiassa pelattavia EM-kisoja jatkuvat Suomen kotiottelulla Espanjaa vastaan Tampereella.

programme.title: Paratiisi (12)
programme.desc: Hilkka (Riitta Havukainen), Andres (Fran Perea) ja Kimi (Asko Vaarala) saapuvat Espanjaan avustamaan Luisaa (Maria Romero). Suomalaisen yrittäjäpariskunnan Sohannan (Alina Tomnikov) ja Petterin (Paavo Kinnunen) omituiset yhteydet herättävät epäilyksiä myös Aurinkorannikon muiden suomalaisten keskuudessa. Vesilaitoksesta tehtävä löytö saa tiimin ymmärtämään, että kyseessä on suurempi rikosvyyhti.

programme.title: YleX Esittää: Battle Beast
programme.desc: Battle Beast -yhtyeen keikka Tuska 2025 -festivaalilta Helsingin Suvilahdesta. Energisistä live-esiintymisistään tunnettu kotimainen Battle Beast on soittanut tinkimättömällä tyylillään tiensä hevifanien sydämiin niin Suomessa kuin maailmalla.

programme.title: Kaamos - suomalaisen metallin viisi vuodenaikaa
programme.desc: Kuinka paljon sä haluat tätä? Traagisista tarinoista ja varoittavista esimerkeistä huolimatta raskas musiikki vaatii usein veronsa. Unelman toteutumisen ja rundaamisen sietämätön raskaus, päihdesekoilut, terveysongelmat ja supertähtien yhteentörmäykset. Hiljaisuuden päättävä sovinto, tosiystävyys, musiikin voima sekä folkmetallin parantava huumori ja sankarienergia. Mukana mm. Battle Beast, Noora Louhimo, Sentenced And Miika Tenkula, Children of Bodom, Bodom After Midnight And Alexi Laiho, Silke Yli-Sirniö, Joel Hokka, Tarja Turunen, Marco Hietala ja Ensiferum. Kertojana Juha Raivio.

programme.title: Lentopallon EM: 2. välieräottelu, kooste
programme.desc: Lentopallon miesten EM-kisojen 2. välieräottelu. Selostus: Johannes Oikarinen, asiantuntijana Timo Tolvanen, Milano, Italia. Koostelähetys.

programme.desc: When a mother and a teenager are evicted from a townhouse in Montreal, the young girl commits suicide.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: A session with a Ouija board transforms Marie's home into a portal for the diabolical. The family realizes that the evil can lurk in the most ordinary places - and in the most innocent people.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Jan's seven-year-old son Cody begins communicating with an imaginary friend who lives in a red box in a nearby cemetery. Feeling helpless and desperate to protect her son, Jan contacts a shaman.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In Taiwan, an American family refuses to believe there are ghosts in their house until their daughter becomes possessed. A Taoist priest explains that their house has been designed to empower the dead.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In Brookfield, Connecticut, young David suffers from intense nightmares and is physically attacked by an invisible entity. Paranormal investigators make contact with a legion of demons inside the child's body.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: An enigmatic photo of her boyfriend's brother killed in Vietnam entrances Lisa. As her obsession grows, she realizes that the spirit of the dead soldier is taking control of their lives.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In a small house in Glen Burnie, Maryland, unseen intruders attack 10-year-old Billy Bean. Billy struggles to learn the secrets of the house and fight them in any way he can - to save his sanity.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: In the far north-east of Georgia, on the border with Russia, the Abano Pass leads to lofty heights. At almost 3000 metres it is the highest passable road in the Great Caucasus. It winds its way up dizzyingly steep slopes. On wild paths, it leads through a fascinating landscape.

programme.title: Dream Islands of Europe: Lanzarote and Fuerteventura
programme.desc: The film presents the two Canary Islands Lanzarote and Fuerteventura. Lanzarote has a rich culture in addition to a volcanic landscape: the film accompanies a ceramic artist, an instrument maker, shows architecture by César Manrique and a camel breeder. On Fuerteventura, in addition to livestock farming and the operation of traditional grain mills, nature conservation plays a major role: islanders are committed to preserving the sand dunes, and there is a turtle hatchery. On Lanzarote, countless volcanic eruptions have formed a bizarre lunar landscape. It is a great challenge for the inhabitants to extract the cultivation of food from the karstic, dry soil. And yet they even manage to produce wine. Protected by thousands of small depressions that act as water reservoirs, they grow vines on porous volcanic rock.

programme.title: mareTV: Sardinia - Magical Island in the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Sardinia is the second-largest island in the Mediterranean. The Sardin-ians themselves say it's a continent for itself, a virtual world of its own, full of magic: A beach, gleaming in unreal pink shades, red corals protect against the evil eye and the inhabitants seem to remain forever young. On Sardinia, the owners of luxury yachts adopt sheep, fish have gold in their bellies and a giant mussel supplies the material for legendary sea silk. No one is surprised, that the Madonna goes on a sea cruise once a year.

programme.title: Women Above the Clouds
programme.desc: Aerobatics is the supreme discipline in air sports. Only a few pilots dare to navigate a machine during loops, drops and steep flights because nausea and blackouts due to the strong G-forces can be life-threatening. But flight instructor Jenny Holmenes is not deterred - she wants to prove her skills. Although she is still a beginner, she competes in the Sportsman class at the Norwegian Aerobatic Championships.

programme.title: Women Above the Clouds
programme.desc: Alaska - the largest and at the same time most sparsely populated state in the USA. Only about 740,000 people live here. Often far away in small villages. Almost every village has its own airstrip. Aircrafts are one of the main means of transport in Alaska. Jamie Klaes is one of the many female pilots in the country.

programme.title: Women Above the Clouds
programme.desc: Alia Twal is an enthusiastic pilot, globetrotter and adventurer. She is a first officer with the Jordanian airline Royal Jordanian and flies large passenger planes. She climbs the highest mountains in the world, dives with sharks or goes skydiving. Alia particularly enjoys travelling in her Jordanian homeland.

programme.title: Moon, The: Our Gateway To The Universe
programme.desc: We are on the verge of a new age of exploration: besides the plans of NASA and other space agencies, over the next years also privately financed teams are going to send unmanned vehicles to the Moon. The goal is to find a cheap and efficient way to travel there on a regular basis, and in the long term to build a permanent human base.

programme.title: Fuerteventura: The golden beauty of the Canaries
programme.desc: Fuerteventura, the second largest of the Canary Islands, is located just 120 kilometres off the coast of West Africa. The climate is extremely dry and the struggle for water has always been a major setback. Then, around a century ago, returning US emigrants brought what were then modern wind turbine water pumps from the Aermotor Windmill Company with them to Fuerte-ventura. Today, the environmentally friendly and so-called “Chicago’s”, experience a renaissance. Unfortu-nately, original spare parts in good condition are diffi-cult to come by. When Leocadio Araya Sanchez began planting countless cacti on a barren hillside a few years ago, people thought he was mad. His idea was to make a healthy juice drink from the prickly pears – with great success. But getting the fruit to release its pre-cious superfood juice is no simple task. On an almost daily basis, Marcos Tapia is magnetically attracted to one of the paradisiacal beaches of the island. The 44-year-old is Spanish champion and vice world champion in para-body board surfing. When he was 28. Marcos was involved in a serious motorbike accident and has been paraplegic ever since.

programme.title: Bosnia Herzegovina
programme.desc: Wild and unknown lies the still undiscovered natural paradise of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the heart of Europe. Rough mountains, dense forests and wild waterfalls characterize the picture of the untouched landscapes. Lynx, wolves and bears roam mountains and valleys. One of the last primeval forests in Europe is a retreat for many endangered animal species. Bosnia and Herzegovina is actually an undiscovered natural paradise in the middle of Europe.

programme.title: Bosnia Herzegovina
programme.desc: The barren, karstic south of the country, Herzegovina, also impresses with its natural landscapes. One of them is the Livno field. Not only is it the largest wetland in the country, it is also the largest regularly flooded karst field in the world. About 700 wild horses live in this unique landscape. Their ancestors were working horses that were abandoned here more than 50 years ago. Another special feature of the karst landscape are the rivers with their tufa barriers. The countless waterfalls that pour over it are a unique natural phenomenon.

programme.title: Menorca - Majorca's beautiful sister
programme.desc: Not nearly as crowded as Majorca or Ibiza: Menorca has noticeably fewer visitors than her sister islands and in 1993, was recognised by UNESCO as a biosphere re-serve. Menorca also has its own distinctive charm, with its secluded coves, mighty cliffs, beautiful gardens and ages old towns and villages. Its residents love the is-lands treasures and peculiarities. Forests make up al-most a third of Menorca, complemented by many lush green meadows. Next to tourism, agriculture is a major source of the island's income to the present day. On Menorca, there are several accumulations of enormous megalithic stones. From a global point of view, the up to five-metre-tall Taulas, whereby the stones are ar-ranged in the shape of a T, are unique.

programme.title: Meteor Menace
programme.desc: On February 15th, 2013, out of the blue, a meteorite exploded in the earth’s atmosphere above the Russian region of Chelyabinsk. The event is a reminder of the ever-present 'Meteor Menace' and the need to understand more about these missiles from outer space.

programme.title: World's Most Dangerous Railway Lines
programme.desc: The Tanzania-Zambia-Railway (Tazara) is one of Africa's most ambitious infrastructure projects. It connects the inland with the coast of East Africa and meant independence from the surrounding apartheid-ruled countries of East Africa. The film accompanies the Tazara on its 52-hour journey through Tanzania and Zambia and uses spectacular aerial shots to show not only the architectural monuments but also the unknown sides of the previously hidden landscapes of Tanzania and Zambia.

programme.title: World's Most Dangerous Railway Lines
programme.desc: Over 196 bridges and through 55 tunnels, the Bernina Express fights its way from Switzerland to Italy. Powerful forces of nature make the railyway line a dangerous route over the Grisons Alps to this day. The film accompanies the Bernina Express in winter over the highest rail route across the Alps.

programme.title: World's Most Dangerous Railway Lines
programme.desc: The Ferrocarril del Sur, one of the highest train routes on earth, runs right through the mountains of Peru. To this day, it is considered a miracle in the world of railways. The rails not only lead to the famous ruined city of Machu Picchu but connect the ancient Inca capital of Cusco with Puno on the shores of Lake Titicaca and the gleaming white city of Arequipa. A train journey with the Andes Explorer through a grandiose landscape and an undeveloped and inaccessible area.

programme.title: mareTV: Estonia's Enchanted Islands - Kihnu, Hiiumaa, Saaremaa And Co
programme.desc: Kihnu is one of 19 inhabited Estonian islands. When the women there ride motorcycles in colourful skirts, it is summer. Thanks to its remoteness, charming traditions have been preserved here. More than 2,000 islands belong to Estonia, none is like the other, each with its own character. Most of them were military restricted areas during the Soviet Union. Of all things, the strict shielding had its good points: beach, forest, juniper groves, they still characterise the landscape of Estonia's enchanted islands. Elly Karjam is a multi-jobber: lighthouse keeper, ice-cream producer and contract knitter for the famous Kihnu sweaters. Summer is high season for her: She is expecting guests from the USA, who had their ancestors on Kihnu. Birches have to be cut for the so-called viht. This bunch of birch branches is an important accessory for the traditional sauna at midsummer. And the motorcycles in the shed are to be refloated.

programme.title: Secrets of the North Sea
programme.desc: The North Sea is enigmatic. It presents itself in cool shades of grey. Yet who would have guessed that beneath the chilly waves are opulent coral gardens, courting squids, and several of the largest sea creatures on the planet?

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Some risks on these car routes have natural causes: Extreme weather, avalanches and landslides. In some areas, the locals even believe that evil spirits kill travelers. But many of the dangers are man-made: robbers or terrorists lie in wait for travelers, and tough labor pressures, social hardship and greedy mass-transit businesses also cause tragic driving accidents around the world. In the 20th century alone, 35 million people died on roads worldwide - plus 1.5 billion injured!

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Roads are much more than just gray strips of asphalt that allow us to travel and trade. For centuries they have been lifelines of mankind, full of stories and history - and in certain countries and areas they also hold great dangers, much human suffering and death. Documentary filmmaker Oliver G. Becker ventured onto dangerous roads in New Zealand, Scotland and Australia for phoenix.

programme.title: The Moor
programme.desc: Moors and peatlands are oases in the cultivated landscape of Central Europe.

programme.title: Eyes Of The Atacama
programme.desc: ALMA – the Atacama Large Millimeter Array – is the ultimate space observation facility. Here, 66 leviathan parabolic antennae trap cosmic rays in the previously unobservable long-wave range. It can only happen in Atacama, far away from civilisation’s pollution of the night sky with artificial light.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.desc: Saguaro National Park is an American national park in Pima County, southeastern Arizona. The 92,000-acre (37,000 ha) park consists of two separate areas—the Tucson Mountain District (TMD) about 10 miles west of the city of Tucson and the Rincon Mountain District (RMD) about 10 miles east of the city—that preserve Sonoran Desert landscapes, fauna, and flora, including the giant saguaro cactus.An inventory of medium and large mammals in the park confirmed the presence of 30 species in Saguaro National Park between 1999 and 2008. Of these, 21 were found in the Tucson Mountain District and 29 in the Rincon Mountain District. A partial list of the park's mammals includes cougars, coyotes, bobcats, white-tailed deer, mule deer, javelinas, gray foxes, black-tailed jackrabbits, desert cottontails, ring-tailed cats, white-nosed coatis, ground squirrels, and packrats. One endangered mammal, the lesser long-nosed bat, lives part of the year in the park and part of the year in Mexico.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.desc: Great Smoky Mountains National Park is an American national park in the southeastern United States, with parts in Tennessee and North Carolina. The park straddles the ridgeline of the Great Smoky Mountains, part of the Blue Ridge Mountains, which are a division of the larger Appalachian Mountain chain. The park contains some of the highest mountains in eastern North America, including Clingmans Dome, Mount Guyot, and Mount Le Conte. The border between the two states runs northeast to southwest through the center of the park. The Appalachian Trail passes through the center of the park on its route from Georgia to Maine. With 12.5 million visitors in 2019, the Great Smoky Mountains National Park is the most visited national park in the United States.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.desc: Yellowstone National Park is an American national park located in the western United States, largely in the northwest corner of Wyoming and extending into Montana, and Idaho. It was established by the U.S. Congress and signed into law by President Ulysses S. Grant on March 1, 1872. Yellowstone was the first national park in the U.S. and is also widely held to be the first national park in the world. The park is known for its wildlife and its many geothermal features, especially Old Faithful geyser, one of its most popular. While it represents many types of biomes, the subalpine forest is the most abundant. It is part of the South Central Rockies forests ecoregion.

programme.title: The Seychelles - Africa with South Seas ambience
programme.desc: The 115 islands and islets that make up the Seychelles present a breath-taking variety of plants, rare animals and beaches laced with palms. This is where the leg-endary Coco de Mer palm nuts grow with fruits weigh-ing up to 20 kilos and giant wild land turtles nibble away at mangrove fruits to their hearts content. The archipelago was first settled at the end of the 18th cen-tury. Today, a very colourful potpourri of peoples in this dwarf state proves just how peacefully different cultures can live side by side. Three times a week, the steamer MV Espoir completes the trip from the main island of Mahé to Praslin and back. A ship for every-one and practically everything: Used cars, toilet paper, horses, bicycles, furniture - you name it, the Espoir transports goods of all kinds. Coconuts sometimes pose a problem as there are far too many of them. What to do with them? The best place to send them is undoubt-edly Hubert Roumien's Virgin Coconut Oil Laboratory, hidden away in the Mahé jungle. Straw turns into gold at Seaweed Seychelles! There, Benjamin Port Louis collects seaweed and extracts liquid fertiliser from it.

programme.title: mareTV: Capri and the Amalfi Coast - Italy's Ocean Legends
programme.desc: Capri was already in ancient times a place for the rich and beautiful. Today Capri is one of the most famous islands in the world. Millions of tourists visit it. But there are in fact still unknown corners on the island in the Gulf of Naples. Thus, at the very top of Capri, there is a hermit monastery with a view to the Vesuvius.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: The racing cyclists of Burundi have a dangerous job. But it’s a vital one for Burundi’s economy. Bicycles are the main means of transportation in one of the smallest countries in Africa. Bananas, the staple food in Burundi, are transported from the markets to a banana beer brewing factory. We accompany Tharcien, a bike courier, on his exhausting cross country trip on the Burundi Highway.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: It is one of the wildest roads in Asia: the Trans Sulawesi Highway. The adventurous road leads through Indonesia's fourth-largest island and takes people to spectacular destinations. To beautiful beaches, turbulent cities, or unique primeval forests.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: Tanzania is known for its national parks, vast landscapes and wild roads. They make traveling a real adventure. We travel in trucks, buses and off-road vehicles from the Indian Ocean via the Serengeti to Lake Victoria, accompany huge herds of wildebeest, observe lions and rhinos - and show the lives of the people who live on and along the roads.

programme.title: Wild Sardinia
programme.desc: Sardinia has always been the epitome of pure wilderness, an emerald of volcanic origin in the Mediterranean. 1900 metres of coastline and an infinite maze of offshore islands. But Sardinia also has other facets: green valleys, rugged mountains, murmuring brooks, mysterious ruins and a unique fauna. Just off of Sardinia's coast is an untouched underwater paradise - uniquely beautiful, but also dangerous. Pilot whales, dolphins and mobula rays populate the waters at Capo Testa in the north of the island. In the west, the lagoons of Cabras represent a wild landscape of lakes in which thousands of flamingos live and hunt the red brine shrimps. In addition to the flamingos, grey and purple herons and little egrets breed here. Thousands of bats have found refuge in the craggy mountain world of the Supramonte and Gennargentu, with their countless grottoes and caves. In the sea we can observe the mass mating of sea slugs, and thanks to our camera robots and submersible boats we were able to observe beard worms with luminous red gills, as well as bright yellow tree corals in the area surrounding the hypothermal lava holes.

programme.title: mareTV: Majorca
programme.desc: Cleaning woman island, concrete castles, Ballermann: Mallorca's image is negatively affected in some respects. The documentary explores the charm of the largest Balearic island beyond the hustle and bustle of tourism and Rambazamba. The real Mallorca is best explored through real Majorcans: Manolo Barahona, TV fishing expert from the local island broadcaster IB3, faces the most difficult task of the year. The Raor is in season, the most expensive fish on the island. Manolo is supposed to get him first in front of the camera and then in the pan. There's only one catch, the little fish with the piranha teeth just doesn't want to be on TV. In the first months of the year Mallorca turns into a sea of almond blossoms. There are around seven million almond trees on the island, once planted to replace dead vines. But now also the almond trees are threatened. The fire bacterium continues to spread, especially on the large plantations. The farmer Biel Torrens wants to save Mallorca's almond trees and fruit with a small organic plantation and gentle harvesting methods. He shakes the almonds from the tree by hand instead of using a mechanical vibrator.

programme.title: Secrets of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: The contours of the Mediterranean have changed during the course of its history. Near Gibraltar, Africa was once connected to the European continent. When the land bridge at Gibraltar collapsed, the Mediterranean basin filled up again. The Suez Canal is today connected to the Red Sea. This route enables animals to reach the Mediterranean, where they cause problems.

programme.title: Secrets of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Rugged rocks, blue sea and idyllic, sandy beaches - this is the Mediterranean as we know it. But this impression is deceptive: the Mediterranean is under constant change. The continents are moving towards one another. Animals, that have to survive under such extreme conditions, must find a way to escape the dangers. Between deserts and volcanoes, the challenges for the animals are enormous.

programme.title: mareTV: Scotland's Mild West - On The Inner Hebrides
programme.desc: The Inner Hebrides surprise with green hills, fine sandy beaches and a mild climate, at least as far as Scottish conditions allow. This is ensured by the currents of the Gulf Stream, as well as the Scottish archipelago being protected by its sister islands, which belong to the Outer Hebrides. More than half of the almost 80 islands are uninhabited. Loneliness has made the people rather inventive. On Tiree Island, mathematics, history and physics from the mainland arrive in the classroom per mouseclick. Dr Mauvis Gore and Prof. Rupert Ormond cast off from the island of Mull, after setting a course to encounter a basking shark. The cetohinus maximus is the world's second largest fish and the two scientists are absolutely convinced that the waters surrounding the Mull constitute the mating grounds for the basking sharks. A logistical challenge takes place on the Isle of Easdale each September. Then, around 400 people populate the tiny slate island. Donals Mellon Melville organises the World Skimming Championships, a World Cup in jumping stones. This is all about the distance they are thrown and they must only hop above the water twice.

programme.title: Countries People Adventures - Iceland Extreme
programme.desc: In southeastern Iceland, Europe's largest glacier, the gigantic Vatnajökull, covers an area of around 9,000 square kilometers. Beneath it lie the world's most active and dangerous volcanoes. This extreme landscape is as dangerous as it is fascinating: glistening white glacier tongues, lagoons covered with icebergs, bizarre green lava mountains, snow-covered volcanic cones, solidified lava flows and imposing waterfalls overwhelm everyone who gets to see them. In 2008, Icelanders declared the glacier and adjacent areas a national park, the largest in Europe. In this documentary, the team meets people who live, work or do research here: a life with the dangers of fire and ice in the overwhelming landscape of Vatnajökull National Park.

programme.title: Legendary Paddle Steamers
programme.desc: Idlewild - Avalon - Belle of Louisville - these three names stand for the last still roadworthy, historic sternwheeler in the USA. In 1914, the ship was built as Idlewild for the West Memphis Packet Company as a passenger ferry. With a draft of only 1.50 m and a robust steel hull, the boat is suitable for almost all navigable rivers of the Mississippi River system. Today, the Belle is the most traveled steamboat in American history. In the course of her eventful life, she has called at 130 places in 19 states.

programme.title: Legendary Paddle Steamers
programme.desc: Lake Lucerne in the heart of Switzerland stretches from the foothills of the Alps to the first three-thousand-meter peaks of the high mountains. Home waters of the paddle steamer Unterwalden. For two and a half years she was not on the water. Now, after the biggest renovation in her history, the life of the 110-year-old paddle steamer is starting all over again. Her first voyages, with all the imponderables and challenges for the crew, take her into a diverse, wild landscape, right into the mystical heart of Switzerland. In their territory, scenic contrasts collide: barren high moorland and gently rolling alpine meadows, modern tourist resorts and quiet mountain villages, caves hidden deep in the earth and snow-covered two-thousand-meter peaks. The Unterwalden is part of the oldest and largest fleet of paddle steamers so high above the sea. Here on Lake Lucerne, according to national legend, the three original cantons swore eternal allegiance to each other over seven hundred years ago. A land around which countless myths entwine and whose lifeline since the opening of the Gotthard Pass in the thirteenth century was the shipping traffic on the lake.

programme.title: Chasing Quakes
programme.desc: Europe has experienced catastrophic earthquakes – even though the 'old continent' is not the most notorious region on Earth for strong quakes, the danger from below is very real. Autumn 2016 tragedy strikes north-central Italy. A series of four earthquakes cracks a mountain and flattens a historic town.

programme.title: mareTV: Newfoundland - Canada's Eastern Point
programme.desc: In Newfoundland, at the easternmost tip of North America, the landscape is pristine, dramatic, and very sparsely populated. In summer, icebergs occasionally drift along the steep cliffs. When the Titanic collided with an iceberg and sank just 300 miles off the coast of Newfoundland in 1912, the last radio messages were picked up in a small wooden hut on the Avalon Peninsula. Today, most Newfoundlanders live on Avalon. There are particularly many seabirds here. In Witless Bay, the newborn puffins are ready for their first descent into the Atlantic. But some stray onto the coastal road, attracted by the lights of the hotels and restaurants. In doing so, they run the risk of being run over. A team of volunteers saves the lives of countless young birds: The Puffin And Petrel Patrol goes out at night dressed in high-visibility vests to collect the puffins. Biologist Sabrina Wilhelm then brings them back to Green Island, home to the largest puffin colony in North America. Here, the birds catch up on what they should have done long ago: the first dive of their lives.

programme.title: The U.S. East Coast
programme.desc: Nowhere is the American way of life as relaxed as on Florida's beaches. The Keys, a chain of islands at the far southern end of the state, reveal a more laid-back side of the USA. But all of Florida amazes -- with secluded beaches, unspoiled nature, and the legacy of the early European settlers.

programme.title: The U.S. East Coast
programme.desc: New Hampshire has only 19 kilometers of coastline and short summers, all the more reason Shauna Fraser takes every opportunity to be by the sea. In the sheltered harbor of Rye, Shauna also targets inner attitude with yoga on a paddleboard.

programme.title: mareTV: Madeira - Portugal's sea of blossoms in the Atlantic Ocean
programme.desc: Flower magic in Madeira: The Flower Festival Festa da Flor is the most important event of the year for the people of the Atlantic island. With it they celebrate spring, which is climatically practically all year round here, their island and themselves. The coast formed by lava, centuries-old laurel forests and green steep slopes make Madeira unique. Those who start right at the front of the big parade of the flower festival in the capital Funchal, will have made it. For Isabel Borges this dream has come true. She opens this year's flower parade along the harbour promenade with her festive group. This accolade does not only mean fame and prestige, but also a lot of pressure. Are the self-designed dresses splendid enough? Will the 150 flower children learn the dance steps in time? Will the flowers on the float hold out in the heat? For Isabel, it is now a matter of nerves.

programme.title: mareTV: Martinique
programme.desc: The island of Martinique is a piece of France in the Caribbean, between Florida and South America. And of course, Savoir-vivre applies just as it does on the other side of the Atlantic, between the English Channel and the Mediterranean. Jacky Pascault is the first and only man to cultivate mushrooms in the Caribbean. Everywhere else, they grow on artificially fertilised soil, but Jacky's Champignons Tropicaux flourish on sugar cane fibres. Nicole Vilo tailors hats and dresses out of coconut palms. Of course, the catwalk for the models wearing her first collection is one of the countless dream beaches. The Martiniquais sail on boats they call Yole, which have no keel and are therefore difficult to navigate. The crew members hang over the water in breakneck fashion on long wooden poles. Just the job for Yole-boss Max' problem kids: they not only learn complicated handling, but also team spirit.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: In the southwest of Portugal lies the little known Parque Natural do Sudoeste Alentejano e Costa Vicentina. It encompasses a narrow coastal strip that runs along the coast to the south of Portugal. Sparsely populated, this coastal region, which was placed under protection in 1988, is considered one of the last intact ecosystems in Europe. The steep cliffs, the almost constant wind and high waves have ensured that mass tourism has not gained a foothold here. There are still near-natural forests and a diverse bird life.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: The highest mountain range in Portugal is the Serra da Estrela. The episode embarks on a voyage of discovery to adventurous rock formations and villages steeped in tradition. The nature park is the largest protected area on the Iberian peninsula. In the mountain range we accompany the young scientist Ana Matos, who wants to breathe new life into old traditions, and cheese maker Maria Natália Lopes. She watches over more than 350 sheeps.

programme.title: Italy My Love
programme.desc: In ten coastal areas of Italy, we encounter people that have a very special relationship with their region. All of them love their country, their traditions and their work. We met with enthusiasts and hedonists that permitted us to take a glimpse into their everyday lives. Young Italians, who have rediscovered nature and its treasures. Others, that preserve the beauty, archaeologists that apply whole new methods, farmers that only cultivate that which the soil needs. Fishermen, who fish in the same way as it was done a century ago and tough, young men who play and dance the Tarantella. Dolphins, giant sea turtles and pink flamingos, which are researched, nursed back to health or simply observed. Cave explorers, sail makers and coffee specialists are also part of the big picture. Flying drone cameras provide birds-eye views and are an important element of the films. The results are spectacular images from completely different angles which provide us with landscape overviews and detailed insights, the likes of which have never been seen before.

programme.title: mareTV: The Caribbean for explorers: St. Vincent and the Grenadines
programme.desc: Much more Caribbean than on the islands of St. Vincent and the Grenadines is hardly possible. Deserted beaches, uninhabited islands, lush vegetation, the 33 islands in total are dreamlike with extremely hospitable inhabitants. Miranda Phillips runs a laundry and water boat on Bequia. Every morning, the 32-year-old navigates from yacht to yacht with her small bright green service vehicle and is already expected by most skippers. Miranda promises radiantly fresh laundry, which she delivers again the same day. And so there is always something going on in her tiny laundrette in the harbour. It turns into a karaoke bar in the evening, because that is Miranda's great passion. Eban Olliver has many jobs at once. He is the lighthouse keeper of Kingstown. And that means a lot of responsibility in St. Vincent's biggest port city. Because Eban doesn't just change the light bulbs, he's a pilot dispatcher, harbour master and guard all in one person. First contact with ships is particularly important. Once he even saved the entire nation from an Ebola virus.

programme.title: Myths of the Congo - Apes and Aliens
programme.desc: The Congo, mighty and deep like no other river - yet still a retreat and a habitat for several of our world's strangest animals. Our closest relatives live deep inside the dense jungles: three of the four giant ape species have made the Congo basin their home. Rich in extraordinary footage, the second episode of Myths of the Congo also presents exciting insights into one of the most mysterious and dangerous regions on earth.

programme.title: Myths of the Congo - Deep and Dangerous
programme.desc: The river that swallows all rivers - this is what the natives call it. In reality, the Congo, when considering its water masses, is the second largest and the deepest river in the world. At its source in the north of Zambia, it starts out as a mere trickle, but on its journey westwards it grows and grows, becoming ever mightier and with it, the animals, too: the shoebill stork hides in the dense papyrus. Metre-long pythons hunt for their prey in trees and huge hippos fight for power and respect in the water. To survive in the Congo, animals have to adapt to extreme conditions. Here, evolution has spawned unique creatures: fish with lungs, wings and those that go hunting on land. The Congo River feeds the second largest rainforest on earth. Here is the home of the forest elephant. Time and again, they are summoned to this one, magic place: the Dzanga Bay. Countless other forest dwellers join them. What makes this place so special?

programme.title: Wild Prairie Man
programme.desc: Located in the Northern Great Plains of Canada, Grasslands National Park has been a 20 year odyssey for wildlife photographer James R. Page. For James, critters are more interesting than people and he shares some of his iconic images and experiences from this endangered ecosystem. We showcase the parks wilderness that is dominated by prairie light and dark sky, the wildlife, prairie dogs, mesmerizing landscapes, and bisons. We immerse ourselves in the wild habitat of Grasslands National Park for over a year capturing some never before scenes in the Wild Prairie. James R. Page's connection to the land and the wildlife provides an unforgettable journey into the heart of this endangered ecosystem, while Park experts help us understand its complexity.

programme.title: Tren Atlantico
programme.desc: We travel by train from the westernmost point of mainland Europe up to Portugal's only national park, the Peneda-Gerês, and from lively Porto to the Spanish border in the northeast. The train takes you from the blue sea to the green Douro Valley, from the urban metropolis to the scorching heat of the deserted hinterland.

programme.title: Tren Atlantico
programme.desc: Switzerland or Spain? This question is often asked by those who see pictures from northern Spain for the first time: High mountains, lonely villages, but - this is the crucial difference - also breathtaking Atlantic beaches. The Costa Verde, the green coast, is a piece of Spain that is so different from the general tourist image of the Germans' favorite vacation destination. This area has been spared from mass tourism. We travel by train from Bilbao in the Basque Country to Santander in Cantabria and Asturias.

programme.title: Rewilding: Back to Nature
programme.desc: Worldwide, there are various projects and approaches to give nature more space again. The aim is to create larger wilderness areas that develop with hardly any influence of humans - by reintroducing so-called key animal species and creating a network of wilderness corridors across entire continents. Rewilding promises to be a cost-effective form of conservation in which we can boost biodiversity and protect the climate.

programme.title: Survival of the Fittest in the Alps
programme.desc: The documentary shows the survival strategies of various animal species in the high mountains of the Alps in winter. Despite freezing temperatures and limited food supply, chamois, red deer and snow hares manage to survive the cold months. Latest research reveals the amazing abilities the animals have developed to adapt to the extreme conditions and also how climate change is altering the behaviour of the alpine inhabitants.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: The Sichuan Tibet Highway is the road of longing for many. It leads through fascinating landscapes and remote areas up to the Himalayan Mountains. We accompany truck driver Ren Taiping on his trip to the Tibetan capital city of Lhasa, encountering pilgrims, mountain bikers and nomads on this dangerous journey.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Malaysia's rice has a secret superpower
programme.desc: Despite its fertile tropical landscape, Malaysia produces only around two-thirds of the rice it needs. Chinese ratoon rice technology is now being applied to lift yields and enhance food security—unlocking new potential for tropical farming. Discover more in CGTN's special series #FarmedwithChina. #Chinavsionary

programme.title: Farmed with China: Vietnam's food trade levels up
programme.desc: How is Vietnam's cassava industry reaching global markets? With technical support and cross-border cooperation with China, one crop is moving up the value chain — from local farms to international supply chains.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Thailand's farms go high-tech
programme.desc: As labor grows scarce, how can the land still yield abundant harvests? China-Thailand cooperation is providing solutions: machines for farmers, jobs in factories, and training for young agricultural engineers. Technology is more than equipment — it brings efficiency and hope.

programme.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!
programme.desc: Rice and prawn grow better together. Prawn loosens the soil and control pests, while rice cleans and oxygenates the water. One field, two harvests. A team from Shanghai Ocean University brought this eco-farming model to Cambodia, helping turn rice paddies into new sources of income.

programme.title: Laos farmers hack one season into many
programme.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. Alongside China-Laos Railway strengthening the supply chain, grain production is also gaining a stronger foundation. Explore the story in CGTN's special series Farmed With China.

programme.title: The AI revolution is here - but are we ready for what comes next?
programme.desc: In this special joint episode of World Economic Forum and CGTN, hosts Robin Pomeroy from World Economic Forum and Guan Xin, CGTN Anchor, sit down with Professor Arun Sundararajan of New York University's Stern School of Business, a member of the WEF AI Governance Alliance and author of The Sharing Economy. They dive into the most pressing questions about artificial intelligence. From the future of employment to the deepening divide over AI governance and technological sovereignty, this conversation brings together perspectives from the US, China, and the global stage on how AI is reshaping economies, societies, and geopolitics.

programme.title: BizTalk: China-US economic And trade watch
programme.desc: Global markets are closely watching the trajectory of China-US economic and trade ties. In this episode of BizTalk, CGTN's Michael Wang speaks with Jiang Wenran, founding director of the China Institute at the University of Alberta, and Lyu Xiang, research fellow at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. They look ahead to how bilateral economic and trade ties could evolve over the next few years.

programme.title: BizPodcast: Rate decision week in focus
programme.desc: The Fed raised rates for the first time in three years, while the Bank of Japan is set to make its move next. With energy prices elevated and inflation pressures persisting, central banks are turning more hawkish. Will tightening continue? And what does it mean for the dollar, yen, renminbi, bond yields, and gold? This week on BizTalk, we take a closer look at the new global rate cycle and its market impact.#BizTalk #BizPodcast

programme.title: Driscoll’s and Yunnan: Growing a blueberry business together
programme.desc: Yunnan Province in southwest China is emerging as a major hub for the blueberry production in the country, thanks to its favorable climate and growing expertise. For U.S. berry company Driscoll's, cooperation with growers in the province is creating new opportunities, from cultivation to sales, as demand for premium blueberries grows in China and across Asia.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Malaysia's rice has a secret superpower
programme.desc: Despite its fertile tropical landscape, Malaysia produces only around two-thirds of the rice it needs. Chinese ratoon rice technology is now being applied to lift yields and enhance food security—unlocking new potential for tropical farming. Discover more in CGTN's special series #FarmedwithChina. #Chinavsionary

programme.title: Farmed with China: Vietnam's food trade levels up
programme.desc: How is Vietnam's cassava industry reaching global markets? With technical support and cross-border cooperation with China, one crop is moving up the value chain — from local farms to international supply chains.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Thailand's farms go high-tech
programme.desc: As labor grows scarce, how can the land still yield abundant harvests? China-Thailand cooperation is providing solutions: machines for farmers, jobs in factories, and training for young agricultural engineers. Technology is more than equipment — it brings efficiency and hope.

programme.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!
programme.desc: Rice and prawn grow better together. Prawn loosens the soil and control pests, while rice cleans and oxygenates the water. One field, two harvests. A team from Shanghai Ocean University brought this eco-farming model to Cambodia, helping turn rice paddies into new sources of income.

programme.title: Laos farmers hack one season into many
programme.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. Alongside China-Laos Railway strengthening the supply chain, grain production is also gaining a stronger foundation. Explore the story in CGTN's special series Farmed With China.

programme.title: 2026 BRICS SUMMIT | New Blueprint of the Global South
programme.desc: The 2026 BRICS Summit takes place on 12-13 September in New Delhi, India. Assembling a distinguished group of senior Chinese and Indian scholars and experts, CGTN Biztalk joins with WION from India launching a special episode of TV panel discussion, to find out how expanded BRICS representation translate into deeper cooperation and a more influential role in global governance.

programme.title: The AI revolution is here - but are we ready for what comes next?
programme.desc: In this special joint episode of World Economic Forum and CGTN, hosts Robin Pomeroy from World Economic Forum and Guan Xin, CGTN Anchor, sit down with Professor Arun Sundararajan of New York University's Stern School of Business, a member of the WEF AI Governance Alliance and author of The Sharing Economy. They dive into the most pressing questions about artificial intelligence. From the future of employment to the deepening divide over AI governance and technological sovereignty, this conversation brings together perspectives from the US, China, and the global stage on how AI is reshaping economies, societies, and geopolitics.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Malaysia's rice has a secret superpower
programme.desc: Despite its fertile tropical landscape, Malaysia produces only around two-thirds of the rice it needs. Chinese ratoon rice technology is now being applied to lift yields and enhance food security—unlocking new potential for tropical farming. Discover more in CGTN's special series #FarmedwithChina. #Chinavsionary

programme.title: Farmed with China: Vietnam's food trade levels up
programme.desc: How is Vietnam's cassava industry reaching global markets? With technical support and cross-border cooperation with China, one crop is moving up the value chain — from local farms to international supply chains.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Thailand's farms go high-tech
programme.desc: As labor grows scarce, how can the land still yield abundant harvests? China-Thailand cooperation is providing solutions: machines for farmers, jobs in factories, and training for young agricultural engineers. Technology is more than equipment — it brings efficiency and hope.

programme.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!
programme.desc: Rice and prawn grow better together. Prawn loosens the soil and control pests, while rice cleans and oxygenates the water. One field, two harvests. A team from Shanghai Ocean University brought this eco-farming model to Cambodia, helping turn rice paddies into new sources of income.

programme.title: Laos farmers hack one season into many
programme.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. Alongside China-Laos Railway strengthening the supply chain, grain production is also gaining a stronger foundation. Explore the story in CGTN's special series Farmed With China.

programme.title: 2026 BRICS SUMMIT | New Blueprint of the Global South

programme.title: The AI revolution is here - but are we ready for what comes next?
programme.desc: In this special joint episode of World Economic Forum and CGTN, hosts Robin Pomeroy from World Economic Forum and Guan Xin, CGTN Anchor, sit down with Professor Arun Sundararajan of New York University's Stern School of Business, a member of the WEF AI Governance Alliance and author of The Sharing Economy. They dive into the most pressing questions about artificial intelligence. From the future of employment to the deepening divide over AI governance and technological sovereignty, this conversation brings together perspectives from the US, China, and the global stage on how AI is reshaping economies, societies, and geopolitics.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.5
programme.desc: In this final episode, Tianran journeys to Nyingchi, known as “Xizang’s Garden.” Here, he experiences the region’s semi-pastoral way of life — feeding yaks, trying his hand at archery, and seeing how tourism is transforming lives in Lulang International Tourist Town. Travelling along National Highway 318, Tianran discovers towering millennia-old cypress trees and rafts through the vast Yani National Wetland Park, before ending the day with a unique spa treatment at a traditional Tibetan hospital.

programme.title: Colors of the Daliang Mountains
programme.desc: In the first episode of our Sichuan Daliang Mountains series, we journey to Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture in Sichuan Province. Setting off from Xichang, the prefectural capital, we first explore Lizhou Ancient Town, the southern gateway of the Southern Silk Road. We then travel to Huili County in the southernmost part of the Daliang Mountains, where we listen to the morning bells and evening drums, try our hand at making green pottery, and pick fresh pomegranates. Finally, we head to the western part of the Greater Liangshan Mountains and step into the mysterious Lugu Lake. We visit a Mosuo family to learn about their unique culture and take part in one of the Mosuo people’s most...

programme.title: The Sea’s Fruits Ep.2
programme.desc: With 18,000 kilometers of coastline, China boasts a wide range of ecosystems and a rich source of marine ingredients. The Sea's Fruits focuses on these small treasures of the sea—how they are caught, cooked, and shared. Told through stories of coming together and saying goodbye, the documentary celebrates the joy of eating and explores people's perspectives on family, friendship, and the natural world.

programme.title: Foodwise: Great Walls of Beijing
programme.desc: The Great Wall of China is a popular tourist destination, but did you know that in Beijing, it's where locals go to unwind? From feasts of tofu made using well-water and fish caught fresh from the reservoir, to bubbling cauldrons of thinly-sliced lamb, the hilly suburbs of Beijing are home to some of the city's best-loved weekend escapes - and they're all by the foot of the Great Wall.

programme.title: Foodwise: How to Order Chinese Food
programme.desc: How do you order Chinese food? What's the best way to pair dishes? And what's up with the naming system? In this episode, hosts Tianran and Eva will give you a crash course on everything from deciphering the menu and choosing the right restaurant, to pairing dishes according to color, aroma, taste, and form, so that by the end of the show, you too can feast your friends like a pro.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-5 Xingyi Quan
programme.desc: In Episode 5, Kleber travels to Shanxi, the birthplace of Xingyi Quan. He follows Master Cao Bing, a traditional Xingyi Quan teacher and modern combat coach, from Taiyuan’s noodle shops to Pingyao’s ancient streets, and from centuries-old vinegar breweries to Guandi temples, exploring Xingyi Quan’s deep links to Shanxi’s merchant culture and history.Master Cao breaks down the core principles of the “Five Elements and Twelve Forms”, and shows in his modern gym how techniques found in Muay Thai and Jiu-Jitsu can be integrated without losing Xingyi Quan’s philosophical core, guided by the mindset of taking only what is essential. Set against ancient sites such as Yongle Palace, this episode...

He follows Master Cao Bing, a traditional Xingyi Quan teacher and modern combat coach, from Taiyuan’s noodle shops to Pingyao’s ancient streets, and from centuries-old vinegar breweries to Guandi temples, exploring Xingyi Quan’s deep links to Shanxi’s merchant culture and history.Master Cao breaks down the core principles of the “Five Elements and Twelve Forms”, and shows in his modern gym how techniques found in Muay Thai and Jiu-Jitsu can be integrated without losing Xingyi Quan’s philosophical core, guided by the mindset of taking only what is essential. Set against ancient sites such as Yongle Palace, this episode...

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.5
programme.desc: In this final episode, Tianran journeys to Nyingchi, known as “Xizang’s Garden.” Here, he experiences the region’s semi-pastoral way of life — feeding yaks, trying his hand at archery, and seeing how tourism is transforming lives in Lulang International Tourist Town. Travelling along National Highway 318, Tianran discovers towering millennia-old cypress trees and rafts through the vast Yani National Wetland Park, before ending the day with a unique spa treatment at a traditional Tibetan hospital.

programme.title: Colors of the Daliang Mountains
programme.desc: In the first episode of our Sichuan Daliang Mountains series, we journey to Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture in Sichuan Province. Setting off from Xichang, the prefectural capital, we first explore Lizhou Ancient Town, the southern gateway of the Southern Silk Road. We then travel to Huili County in the southernmost part of the Daliang Mountains, where we listen to the morning bells and evening drums, try our hand at making green pottery, and pick fresh pomegranates. Finally, we head to the western part of the Greater Liangshan Mountains and step into the mysterious Lugu Lake. programme.title: The Sea’s Fruits Ep.2
programme.desc: With 18,000 kilometers of coastline, China boasts a wide range of ecosystems and a rich source of marine ingredients. The Sea's Fruits focuses on these small treasures of the sea—how they are caught, cooked, and shared. Told through stories of coming together and saying goodbye, the documentary celebrates the joy of eating and explores people's perspectives on family, friendship, and the natural world.

programme.title: Aerial China III Ep.1
programme.desc: Yunnan straddles the Hengduan Mountains and Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau, revealing Kawagarbo Peak, vibrant Lijiang, and Hani's golden terraces. Come fly with us on a quest for the essence of Yunnan and discover why it so richly deserves its name - Yunnan, 'the Land South of the Clouds'!

programme.title: Foodwise: Eat Like Confucius
programme.desc: Foodwise host Tianran He explores the ancient town of Qufu, the birthplace of Confucius. Together with a 75th generation descendant of the sage himself, they explore one of Confucius' lifelong pursuits: To cultivate oneself for the betterment of others. From the sophisticated cooking techniques and dining etiquette of Confucian cuisine, which was used for banqueting emperors and aristocrats, to getting hands on with street food and local delicacies, Tianran explores how Confucius' ideals have permeated through modern day life in Qufu.

programme.title: Foodwise: The Herbal Way of Life
programme.desc: 'Medicine tonic is not as good as food tonic' - this Chinese saying is a core principle of Traditional Chinese Medicine. It is believed that the right diet and nourishment can cure and reverse the effects of disease, hence considered an inevitable source of natural health preservation. In this Foodwise episode, our hosts Tianran He and Eva May explore this ancient concept of medicine food homology as they taste their way through different herbs, chat to experts of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and visit venues that combine conventional principles with modern ideas. Dive deep into the origin of TCM with us as we learn about the harmony between man and nature and its application in...

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-6 Shandong Mantis Style
programme.desc: The final episode traces the cross-ocean transmission of Shandong Mantis Style. In the mountains of northern Italy, host Kleber visits Dante Basili, a veteran Italian practitioner in his sixties, who recounts travelling to China 36 years ago to learn Mantis Style and returning home to teach Chinese martial arts ever since.Kleber then heads to Shandong to meet Yu Bo and Yu Tao, sons of Mantis Style grandmaster Yu Hai. He witnesses a traditional apprenticeship ceremony and explores the style’s fighting essence: adopting its spirit rather than merely copying its form. The episode shows how Mantis Style has taken root and flourished in different cultural settings. Ultimately, this journey...

programme.title: China Bound: Xiamen
programme.desc: What's it like in one of China's happiest cities? Tianran is in sunny Xiamen on China's southeast coast, visiting the city's famous island of music and sampling local delicacies like shark meatballs, shacha noodles and fish in soy sauce water. He'll discover former fishing villages turned hipster havens, drink tea with locals beneath traditional tenement buildings, and visit a student enclave brimming with creative startup energy.

programme.title: Fiery Tales of the Daliang Mountains
programme.desc: In this episode, our host takes you to Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture in Sichuan Province, to celebrate the most traditional Torch Festival with the local Yi people. Water nourishes the farmland; fire brings light and warmth. Water and fire are the two essential elements that sustain the life of the Yi people. Puge County is known as the birthplace of the Yi Torch Festival. Our host travels across mountains to the remote heart of Puge County, in search of the origins of the Yi torch, to learn about local daily life, explore the profound Yi culture, and visit a Yi family to share a special “reunion dinner” on the eve of the Torch Festival—just like their own New Year's Eve feast....

programme.desc: For thousands of years, people have been fascinated by the night sky. Through their observations, reflections and questions concerning the origins of the moon and stars, they have sought to understand the nature of the eternal struggle between finite life and the vastness of the universe. The knowledge that life has its limits while knowledge knows no bounds is inherent in the Chinese nation. Bai Jikai is a senior photojournalistwith Beijing Daily, who has focused on filming the night sky for the past 30 years. He believes that it is always possible to break through the limitations of time and space and transcend the obstacle of distance, and that this allows us to perceive the eternal...

programme.desc: For thousands of years, people have been fascinated by the night sky. Through their observations, reflections and questions concerning the origins of the moon and stars, they have sought to understand the nature of the eternal struggle between finite life and the vastness of the universe. The knowledge that life has its limits while knowledge knows no bounds is inherent in the Chinese nation. Bai Jikai is a senior photojournalistwith Beijing Daily, who has focused on filming the night sky for the past 30 years. He believes that it is always possible to break through the limitations of time and space and transcend the obstacle of distance, and that this allows us to perceive the eternal...

programme.title: Foodwise: Eat Like Confucius
programme.desc: Foodwise host Tianran He explores the ancient town of Qufu, the birthplace of Confucius. Together with a 75th generation descendant of the sage himself, they explore one of Confucius' lifelong pursuits: To cultivate oneself for the betterment of others. From the sophisticated cooking techniques and dining etiquette of Confucian cuisine, which was used for banqueting emperors and aristocrats, to getting hands on with street food and local delicacies, Tianran explores how Confucius' ideals have permeated through modern day life in Qufu.

programme.title: Foodwise: Xilingol
programme.desc: The Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region is located in the northern part of China, stretching from northeast to southwest side. In Xilin Gol, the horses, sheep and cows could be found every where. The local cuisines here are so attractive to the tourists, such as the roasted lamb is a traditional local dish. And the fired stone fried lamb is so hard to find if you are not traveling to Inner Mongolia. Have you ever tried salted milk tea? Just join in this visual trip！

programme.title: Foodwise: Kunming
programme.desc: Join host Tianran He in Kunming, the capital of Yunnan province in southwest China. Named the Spring City for its perennially good weather, Kunming is one of China's most ethnically diverse cities, something that's reflected in its food: From boozy sticky rice for breakfast, to the famous Crossing the Bridge rice noodles, and evening barbecues, there's plenty on offer here. Also, it's mushroom season, and Tianran is taking to the hills to hunt for wild fungi – but he'll need a trusty friend to steer him away from the poisonous ones!

programme.title: Ride the trails, unlock Chongli's rhythm
programme.desc: Chongli in Zhangjiakou, north China's Hebei Province, first made its name with Winter Olympic ski runs. Now, with cool summers and a wealth of outdoor activities, this mountain town is writing a new summer chapter. CGTN host Julian Waghann and Mexican traveler Juan Carlos Cheang Guzman came to explore. They tried mountain biking and discovered the sustainable model of winter skiing, summer cycling. At an ultra-trail race, runners pressed forward through pouring rain, their headlamps flickering like stars across the night. The Olympics may have ended, but the venues are far from dormant. They power new vitality for Chongli's all-season sports and cultural tourism.
